messages:
incident-bot: :loud_sound: PAGER: Elevated 5xx across smart-routing policy (cross-region). Symptoms: inter-region fallback churn, increased tail latency. Auto-escalate to on-call.

rachel: jumping in. I see a recent admin action: cluster-level `force-region` for eu-west at 1971008540. That could explain traffic stickiness to eu-west nodes.

tom: yep that command came from a manual mitigation 8m ago to move cust-77 off a degraded us-central cluster. Command: `redwoodctl routing force --scope=cluster --region=eu-west --reason='cust-77 emergency'`. Did that also enable sticky routing by default?

priya: by default cluster-force flips sticky=true when applied, unless `--no-sticky` used. So other traffic may be getting bound to eu-west and then falling back to other regions when capacity hits limits -> bounce.

ben: current behavior: requests destined for eu-west overflow -> fallback to us-central -> policy sees those new mappings and rebinds back to eu-west due to sticky counts, creating a loop. We have metric spike: fallback.count increased x4 in last 5m.

mai: but the original intent was limited: only cust-77 should have moved. Did we forget to create a customer-scoped override?

rachel: looks like an operator shortcut. I can make a per-customer override now. Plan: 1) create customer-scoped override for cust-77, 2) remove cluster force, 3) temporarily turn off cross-region sticky learning, 4) invalidate region routing caches.

sanjay (oncall-1): I'll take watch after mitigation. Handing off in ~20m.

priya: creating override: `redwoodctl routing override create --customer=cust-77 --region=eu-west --model=fast-lex-v3 --scope=customer --reason='preserve emergency action'`

*priya runs command*

priya: override created.

rachel: now removing cluster force: `redwoodctl routing rollback --id=force-1971008540` (safe rollback, no immediate reassign).

*tom runs rollback*

tom: rollback executed. Monitoring routing table convergence.

incident-bot: Alert update: fallback.count trending down 70% -> still seeing ~2% error rate in sessions stuck mid-KV.

ben: residual errors are from stale per-session assignment metadata. We'll clear per-session routing metadata for affected nodes: `redwoodctl session clear --region=eu-west --filter=stuck`

mai: done. sessions cleared.

rachel: also disabling sticky learning at policy level while we stabilize:
```
redwoodctl policy update --id cross-region-routing \
  --set learning.sticky=false --apply-no-restart
```

rachel: applied.

incident-bot: latency 95th reduced from 2.2s -> 1.1s; errors down to 0.8%.

priya: customer impact: cust-12 and cust-77 saw degraded chat responses and occasional 502s. Support notified; engineering can provide a follow-up note with timeline.

ben: short-term mitigations done. Post-incident actions proposed:
- block cluster-level `force-region` without explicit `--no-sticky` flag (safety check)
- add a guardrail that prompts for `--scope=customer` when `--reason` contains 'customer'
- instrument sticky-learning counters and alert at low thresholds
- automate session metadata cleanup on rollback paths

mai: filing tickets: INC-4621 (force-region guardrail), INC-4622 (sticky metrics alert), INC-4623 (auto-session-clean).

sanjay (oncall-1): handing off. I'll watch dashboard for 1 hour. If stable, close in 60m.

rachel: assigning postmortem owner: rachel. Draft due tomorrow EOD. Include timeline, command audit, and proposed guardrails.

priya: support note: short message sent to affected customers with apology and ETA for full recovery.

incident-bot: incident mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: mitigated.

ben: quick reminder: when doing manual migration for a single customer, prefer per-customer override or use `--no-sticky`.

mai: thanks team. no page for now.

sanjay (oncall-1): acknowledged, taking watch.
